title: Thin-client action streams — PRD sketch
body:
Goal
Provide a minimal-density, thin-client pattern for building low-latency interactive features on top of the Hosted API that: 1) supports incremental streaming responses, 2) integrates explicit tool/action calls with graceful fallback, and 3) returns structured, machine-parseable output frames suitable for small SDKs (mobile/web) that must keep memory/CPU low.

Context and motivation
Teams building real-time assistants and embedded copilots increasingly target low-power clients (mobile, browser tab, edge devices). They need: predictable tail latency, incremental partial outputs to render UI quickly, explicit “action” frames so the client can invoke local or cloud tools, and a simple SDK surface that minimizes event loop/connection complexity. Existing Hosted API docs and PRDs focus on rich SDKs and flexible streaming modes. This sketch explores an intentionally thin client pattern: a single streaming connection with a small, typed frame vocabulary that clients can implement without heavy dependency trees.

Top-level requirements
- Incremental output: deliver tokens in ordered frames so UI can append/replace text progressively within 50–200ms typical chunk latency on median path.
- Action/tool frames: allow the model to emit a deterministic action invocation (tool call) with explicit schema and versioning, followed by optional confirmation or retraction frames.
- Structured payloads: all non-freeform content uses simple JSON-LD-like envelopes with type and version fields to simplify client parsing and forward/backward compat.
- Backward compatibility/fallback: clients and servers must handle unknown frame types gracefully; server should include fallback textual summary for older clients.
- Single connection ergonomics: one WebSocket/SSE/HTTP2 stream per session; client should only need to maintain a single handler for all frame types.
- Low memory footprint: avoid large in-memory buffers, support resumable fragments for reconnects, and limit in-flight partial state.

Success metrics
- UI time-to-first-token: < 200ms median for edge regions listed in SLAs.
- Action-confidence false-positive rate < 1% on a labeled eval set.
- SDK adoption: first-party small JS/Swift/Kotlin thin-client libs implemented with < 300 LOC each.
- Error surface: % of client-visible truncated/malformed frames < 0.2% in production over 30 days.

User stories
- As a mobile product engineer, I want the assistant to display partial text while tokens stream so the user perceives immediate progress.
- As an integrations engineer, I want the model to request a user-authorized calendar write using a typed action frame so I can call my backend endpoint deterministically.
- As an SDK maintainer, I want a single event handler for frames so the SDK stays tiny and easy to audit.
- As a platform engineer, I want the server to fall back to plain text for unknown clients so older apps keep working without special updates.

Non-goals
- This PRD does NOT introduce a fully-featured state synchronization protocol (we only support resume tokens and basic fragment replay).
- It does not replace richer SDKs that expose structured tool graphs or advanced typed bindings. This is intentionally minimal.

Frame model (thin vocabulary)
- frame.type: one of ["meta", "text", "action_request", "action_result", "structured_chunk", "end", "error"].
- frame.id: client-assigned or server-assigned id string for de-dup and resume.
- frame.seq: monotonic integer for ordering within stream.
- frame.body: short string or small JSON payload.
- frame.schema_version: semantic version to allow rolling upgrades.

Examples (client subscription semantics)
- Client opens a single WS/SSE connection: sends start message with session_id, client_sdk=\"thin-client-js/0.1\" and preferences (max_tokens, response_mode=\"progressive\").
- Server responds with an initial meta frame: {type: \"meta\", id: \"m1\", seq: 0, body: {model: \"rw-infer-small-v2\",schema_version: \"1.0.0\"}}
- Server streams text frames: {type: \"text\", id: \"t1\", seq: 1, body: {delta: \"The first sentence\"}} Clients append deltas in order.
- Server emits an action_request: {type: \"action_request\", id: \"a1\", seq: 8, body: {action: \"create_calendar_event\", args: {title: \"Sync call\", start: \"2025-12-02T16:00:00Z\"}, spec_version: \"2025-09-01\"}}
- Client receives action_request and either: 1) prompts user and calls backend, then sends an action_result confirmation frame back to server, or 2) rejects and sends action_result with status: \"rejected\".

Action contract rules
- All action_request frames must contain a spec_version and a human_readable_summary string for fallback UI.
- Action argument schema should be small and strongly typed; prefer flat key-value maps with ISO timestamps and op codes.
- Action_result must include status: [\"ok\", \"error\", \"rejected\"] and optional result_payload.
- No embedding of large binary blobs in frames; reference URLs for larger artifacts with time-limited tokens.

Structured output and progressive fidelity
- When model emits structured data (e.g., JSON object representing an API call), it should be delivered as structured_chunk frames with incremental diffs when possible.
- structured_chunk.body will contain: {patch_type: \"append|replace|patch\", payload: <small JSON fragment>, full: boolean}.
- Clients apply patches to reconstruct the current logical object. If patch fails (out-of-order, missing seq), client should request a resume with last_seq and server should re-send canonical state in meta or structured_chunk with full=true.

SDK ergonomics (thin-client principles)
- Single shipped callback: onFrame(frame). Optional helpers: parseFrame, resumeFrom(seq), sendActionResult. Keep SDK < 300 LOC.
- Default behavior: auto-append text frames into a shallow buffer (configurable max_buffer_chars). Developers can opt out to handle raw frames.
- Light-weight reconnection: SDK exposes resumeToken and will attempt N quick reconnects (backoff) to resume stream by specifying last_seq seen.
- Minimal dependency policy: SDKs should avoid heavy JSON5 or binary libs; use built-in JSON and a 1-file transport shim.

Server-side behaviors and guarantees
- Ordering and replay: Server ensures seq monotonicity per session and retains recent segments for resume window (configurable, default 30s / last 500 seqs).
- Fallbacks: If client SDK unknown or older schema_version, include human_readable_summary along each action_request.
- Safety filter: action_request frames go through an action-safety classifier. If confidence < threshold, action is emitted as suggested_text frame + action_request with flagged=true.

Rollout plan
- Stage 1 (internal alpha, 4 weeks): implement server framing, JS thin-client prototype, and run internal integration with two product teams (assistant, docs bot).
- Stage 2 (beta, 8 weeks): expose as opt-in feature for existing endpoints; collect metrics, low-traffic customers. Create Swift/Kotlin thin-client ports.
- Stage 3 (GA): promote to default for 'progressive' response_mode for small clients; provide migration docs and ergonomic samples.

Open questions / trade-offs
- Resume window size vs memory cost on servers. Proposal: default 30s/500 seqs; allow dedicated customers to bump limits.
- How aggressive should safety classifier gating be for action_requests? Too strict reduces usefulness, too permissive risks leaking tool surfaces. Need a labeled eval.
- Should action invocation require an explicit client ACK before server proceeds? That adds complexity to stream but provides stronger semantics for side-effects. For thin-client, prefer best-effort with explicit result frames.

Acceptance criteria for GA
- End-to-end demo from mobile client: streaming text + calendar creation action with user-ack, under 200ms median time-to-first-token in 3 test regions.
- SDKs published to npm/CocoaPods/Maven with MIT license and < 300 LOC each.
- Telemetry: frame error rate under thresholds, action false-positive below target.

Notes to self / next steps
- Pair with runtime team for resume token and seq enforcement interface (runtime API JIRA-PROD-4392).
- Draft concise developer quickstart (one page) with code snippets and UX guidance for action confirmations.
- Run a small user study with partner apps to validate that single-handler model is intuitive.

References and related docs
- Incremental-output-adaptor PRD (review for API overlap).
- Session resume spec (SRE/serving-runtime alignment doc).

Changelog
- 2025-11-04 initial draft by Maya Chen
- 2025-11-18 revised framing semantics after sync with runtime
- 2025-12-02 added structured_chunk patching and rollout plan

TODO
- Add more concrete payload examples (calendar, file-create, search-query)
- Create a small integration test harness to validate seq/resume behavior

---
Internal note: this sketch intentionally biases toward a tiny surface that product teams can implement quickly. If teams need richer ergonomics, we should maintain the richer SDKs separately and provide compatibility layers.
